subject_id.notes: No individual subject identifiers reported in main text; per-subject data referenced only in Supplementary Table 1, not provided.

sample_id.notes: No per-sample identifiers reported in main text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the body of the paper text.

subcohort.notes: The study defines multiple comparison groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US) which are treated as subgroups rather than a single subcohort field.

target_condition.notes: Study is a comparative microbiome characterization, not a disease/condition-focused study; no target condition specified.

control.notes: No case-control design; groups compared are lifestyle-based (traditional vs urban), not disease case/control.

country.evidence_quote: the Matses from the Peruvian Amazon (n = 24)
country.notes: Country for Tunapuco not explicitly named, only 'Andean highlands' mentioned.

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
body_site.notes: Directly stated for Yanomami/Brazil; inferred for other groups as all datasets are gut microbiome/stool-derived per the comparative design.

days_from_first_collection.notes: Single stool sample collected; no longitudinal timepoints reported.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: two hunter–gatherer communities [Yanomami from Venezuela, n = 8; Matses, n = 24], a rural agricultural community [Tunapuco, n = 12], and urban populations [United States, n = 44]
lifestyle.notes: US surface form 'urban populations' does not map directly to an allowed lifestyle enum value.

location.evidence_quote: Satellite image of a Yanomami village in the Brazilian Amazon

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; study is gut microbiome focused.

westernized.evidence_quote: an urban-industrialized group ... and other traditional groups from the Amazon
westernized.notes: Traditional groups described as non-impacted by urban-industrialized lifestyles; US explicitly described as urban-industrialized.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA ® SPIN Kit (MP Biomedicals)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Only reported for the newly generated Yanomami/Brazil dataset; other datasets are from previously published studies not detailed here.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq ® 2500 sequencer
sequencing_platform.section: Methods — DNA Extraction, Library Preparation, and Sequencing
sequencing_platform.notes: Other datasets described only generically as 'sequenced on Illumina platforms' without specific instrument model.

age.evidence_quote: age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired. These details are summarized in Supplementary Table 1
age.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
age.notes: Age data referenced but not provided in main text (only in Supplementary Table 1, not included).

ancestry.notes: No explicit ancestry classification given using ontology terms; ethnic group names (Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco) used instead.

sex.evidence_quote: did not reveal any statistically significant differences in the gut microbiome of female and male Yanomami/Brazil individuals
sex.notes: Both sexes present among Yanomami/Brazil participants but no per-individual sex breakdown or counts given in main text.

age_min.notes: Age/gender data were collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not in the provided text.

age_max.notes: Age/gender data were collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not in the provided text.

age_years.notes: Age/gender data were collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not in the provided text.

dietary_restriction.notes: Diet composition is described qualitatively (fruits, fiber, sylvatic animals) but no formal dietary restriction category is reported.

disease.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease.notes: This statement describes the population generally, not confirmed clinical status of the 15 sampled individuals; inferred with low confidence.

feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal samples were collected for shotgun metagenomic analysis, but no specific stool phenotype measurement is reported.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Neisseria and Desulfovibrio were defined as Yanomami/Venezuela biomarkers, while Klebsiella was the biomarker of the Matses group
biomarker_name.notes: Compiled from multiple sentences across Results and Discussion listing taxonomic biomarkers (genera) identified via LEfSe/LDA analysis for each traditional group.

biomarker_unit.notes: Biomarkers reported as taxa/genera identified by LDA score (>4.0 threshold), no quantitative unit (e.g., abundance %) reported per biomarker.

biomarker_value.notes: No specific numeric LDA scores or abundance values given per biomarker genus; only threshold (LDA score of >4.0) reported as method criterion.

disease_response_os.notes: Study is a microbiome characterization study; no survival/disease response data reported.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; this is a gut microbiome ecology study, not a clinical/oncology study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No specific feces phenotype measurement values (e.g., consistency scores) were reported; only that fecal samples were collected.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

This paper is a gut microbiome/metagenomic study of Yanomami hunter-gatherers and does not report most clinical/demographic fields in the schema (age, BMI, disease status, treatment, etc.) within the main text; such details, if collected, are only referenced as being in Supplementary Table 1 which was not provided.

The 'disease' field value 'Healthy' was inferred from a general statement about the Yanomami population lacking modern chronic diseases, not from direct clinical assessment of the specific 15 sequenced participants; confidence set to low.

This paper is a gut microbiome ecology/metagenomics study, not a clinical oncology or disease-response study; many schema fields (disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size measurements) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
